text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on /v1/stream (continuous-batching path) in us-west2. Current p99 = 2.4s (SLO 1.0s). Paging on-call. Auto-mitigation suggested: route fallback -> low-latency model variant.

dave-oncall: I’m on it. Observed spike started ~2938456108. Streaming stalls + tail amplification when batch sizes hit 64+ for mixed seqlen requests.

sam-sre: Confirming. Traces show heavy KV cache evictions and one GPU with >90% RPC queuing. p95 is 850ms but p99 jumps during these bursts.

alice-runtime: Dumping relevant log slice:```
[2026-03-14T20:02:28Z] req=0x7f3 streaming.start seq_len=12 max_batch=128 packed=1
[2026-03-14T20:02:28Z] scheduler.enqueue batch_id=242 size=60 seq_dist=[2,3,50,6,...]
[2026-03-14T20:02:29Z] kvcache.evict keys=420 pressure=0.82
[2026-03-14T20:02:29Z] run.on_gpu duration=2100ms tail_idx=59
```

jess-cs: Any customer impact? I see a handful of 5xxs reported in dashboard (low volume) but multiple streaming clients reported stalls. Two paid customers in EU are seeing timeouts.

maria-product: Flagging: one internal metric alert also tripped for model-version skew. Could be recent packing change from yesterday deploy.

dave-oncall: Mitigation plan (fast path): 1) flip route to low-latency variant for /v1/stream traffic for priority customers, 2) reduce max_batch_tokens for streaming to 32, 3) enable preemptive-shed for contbatch.

sam-sre: I can execute (2) and (3) now. Commands:```bash
# reduce max_batch_tokens for route
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" "https://control-plane/api/routes/streaming/config" -d '{"max_batch_tokens":32}'
# enable preemptive shed
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/flags" -d '{"contbatch_preemptive_shed":true}'
```

dave-oncall: Do it. Also temporarily pin routing policy to prefer dedicated nodes in us-west2 (bypass packer).

alice-runtime: Applying route config now. Watch logs for backpressure easing.

infra-bot: deploybot: config-change accepted by control-plane (tx=0x9ef). Rolling to us-west2 control-plane pods (3/3).

sam-sre: Preemptive shed ON, max_batch_tokens=32 pushed. Early telemetry: p99 dropped to ~1.1s, p95 stable at 700ms. Still some tail outliers.

dave-oncall: Good. Next: investigate packing policy change from last deploy. @maria-product can you confirm which packaging PR landed yesterday?

maria-product: PR #4823 changed packer to be more aggressive with heterogeneous batching (pack up to 128 if tokens<64). I’m rolling that back from prod-to-qa.

alice-runtime: Adding a short-term scheduler tweak: enforce fairness window 150ms and limit pack_size to 48 for streaming route. Posting command:```json
{
  "route": "/v1/stream",
  "scheduler": {
    "fairness_window_ms": 150,
    "max_pack_size": 48
  }
}
```

sam-sre: Scheduler tweak live. Observability: queue tail reduced, p99 = 0.95s now for us-west2. Customer 5xxs cleared. Marking immediate incident as mitigated.

dave-oncall: Nice work. Action items: - Maria rollback PR and create a follow-up that adds stricter heuristics for mixed seqlen packing - Add a regression test with synthetic mixed-length streaming traffic - Ops: consider a dynamic low-latency override for routes with premium customers.

jess-cs: I’ll notify affected customers and confirm no lasting data loss.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity reduced to S2. Pager cleared for on-call rotation in 30m unless regression.

sam-sre: Postmortem notes starter: root cause = aggressive heterogeneous packer tweak + scheduling fairness gap under mixed sequence loads => Kv cache thrash + local GPU queuing -> tail latency amplification. Short-term fix = reduce batch tokens + fairness window + preemptive-shed. Long-term = packer heuristics + targeted canary + workload-aware autoscaling.

dave-oncall: I’ll take ownership of the postmortem and assign follow-ups. Closing thread after write-up. :white_check_mark:
